Is Koh Samui or Koh Phangan better? | Koh Samui is better for comfort, short trips, families and anyone who wants a direct flight, private hospitals and a wide choice of hotels. Koh Phangan is better for the Full Moon and Half Moon parties, yoga and quieter, wilder beaches. Phangan is only 20–50 minutes from Samui by boat, so you can easily visit one from the other.
Which island is best for families? | Koh Samui. It has the only airport of the three, short transfers, calm bays such as Choeng Mon, supermarkets, several private hospitals and many family resorts. Koh Phangan's quiet north suits families who want a slower pace; Koh Tao is better for older children who snorkel.
Which island is best for diving? | Koh Tao, with the most dive schools, the cheapest courses (an Open Water course costs about 14,000 THB if you start on Tao) and short boat rides to most sites. From Samui, dive day trips go to Sail Rock and Koh Tao from about 4,650 THB for two dives.
Can I visit Koh Phangan and Koh Tao from Koh Samui? | Yes. Koh Phangan is 20–50 minutes away by scheduled boat or private speedboat, and Koh Tao 1 h 30–2 h by fast boat. Our Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan speedboat day trip (2,200 THB, 8–9 hours) and the Full Moon Party speedboat (1,400 THB return) both start and finish on Samui.
Does Koh Phangan have an airport? | No. Koh Phangan has no operating airport, so you arrive by boat, usually from Koh Samui (20–50 minutes), Surat Thani's Donsak pier or Koh Tao. The quickest route from Bangkok is a flight to Samui followed by a boat.
Which island is cheapest? | Koh Phangan and Koh Tao generally have cheaper rooms and more budget bungalows than Koh Samui, which is the dearest of the three mainly because of flights and resorts. Day-to-day costs such as street food and massages are similar on all three, and Koh Tao is the cheapest place to learn to dive.
Do the three islands have the same weather? | Yes. All three are in the Gulf of Thailand: driest and calmest from February to April, warm with short showers from May to September, and wettest from October to December with the north-east monsoon, peaking in November. That is the opposite of Phuket and Krabi.
How many days should I spend on each island? | As a guide: Koh Samui 5–7 days, Koh Phangan 3–5 days (or one night for the Full Moon Party), and Koh Tao 3–4 days, or longer for a dive course. With a week or less, base yourself on Samui and visit the others on day trips.
